guides.title: Clean coils, pans, drains, and exposed surfaces
guides.summary: Use HVAC CR for compatible grease and organic soils; review HVAC HCR for mineral scale. Match the cleaner to the soil and equipment.
guides.prepare: Read the supplied label and SDS. Confirm coil metal, coatings, seals, and the equipment maker's cleaning limits. Isolate power and protect controls; arrange rinse-water capture.

steps.title: Inspect and test
steps.detail: Photograph the buildup and check drainage. Test the selected product on a small inconspicuous area at the approved dilution; inspect for discoloration, coating loss, and seal changes.

steps.title: Mix for this job
steps.detail: Use the current label's dilution and mixing order. Record product, water-to-product ratio, batch volume, and planned contact time. Surface-cleaning ratios are not recirculation doses.

steps.title: Apply and keep control
steps.detail: Apply by the equipment-approved method. Keep cleaner away from energized parts. Observe the label contact time, keep the surface from drying, and use only tools that will not damage fins or coatings.

steps.title: Rinse and inspect
steps.detail: Rinse by the approved method, capture runoff, and inspect fins, pan, drain, and seals. Check that the drain flows and no cleaner residue remains before restoring equipment.

guides.stop: Stop for leaks, discoloration, coating damage, blocked drainage, or unexpected reaction. Do not mix cleaners or use cleaning instructions as a disinfectant procedure.
guides.record: Save before/after photos, dilution, contact time, rinse method, drain check, and any equipment defects.

guides.title: Descale an isolated exchanger or water-side loop
guides.summary: Plan a temporary cleaning circuit using HVAC HCR or Descaler after confirming scale type and compatibility.
guides.prepare: Have a qualified technician approve the method. Confirm metallurgy, gaskets, coatings, isolated volume, pump/hose compatibility, venting, working pressure, concentration, temperature, contact time, monitoring intervals, rinse limits, and waste route before starting.

steps.title: Baseline and isolate
steps.detail: Record flow, pressure drop, inlet/return temperatures, and visible scale. Shut down under the site's energy-control procedure, verify isolation, release stored pressure, cool as required, and protect adjacent operating equipment.

steps.title: Build and water-test the circuit
steps.detail: Connect the cleaning reservoir to a compatible pump, the isolated asset, and a contained return. Use the approved vent arrangement; do not seal a circuit that can evolve gas. Test with water for leaks, flow, return capacity, and isolation from the live system.

steps.title: Charge the approved solution
steps.detail: Measure the actual cleaning volume, including reservoir and hoses. Prepare the specified product concentration using its label mixing order. Do not extrapolate surface dilution or add a second chemical to the circuit.

steps.title: Circulate and log
steps.detail: Run at the approved flow, temperature, and pressure. Log elapsed time, supply/return pH, flow, pressure drop, temperature, and visible reaction at the method's intervals. Filter or remove dislodged solids as specified. Replenish only within the approved method; pH alone does not prove cleaning is complete.

steps.title: Drain and rinse
steps.detail: Stop at the approved endpoint or time limit. Collect spent solution for the site's wastewater assessment. Flush with approved water until the specified pH, conductivity, and residue limits are met; inspect strainers and check flow/pressure drop.

steps.title: Restart and hand off
steps.detail: Restore valves, probes, strainers, and guards; leak-test and return the system under the equipment maker's restart procedure. Re-establish the approved treatment program. Verify operating readings and obtain the owner's acceptance.

guides.stop: Stop circulation for a leak, loss of flow, blocked return, excessive pressure/temperature, uncontrolled gas or foam, or signs of material attack. Never run a cleanout through an occupied or live potable-water circuit.
guides.record: Keep the circuit sketch, isolated volume, product/batch, concentration, readings, waste disposition, rinse acceptance, restored operating data, and owner sign-off.

guides.title: Clean a cooling tower during a planned shutdown
guides.summary: Separate physical cleaning, descaling, and the site's disinfection procedure before restarting treatment.
guides.prepare: Coordinate the outage with the owner and water-management team. Follow the tower maker's instructions and site water-management plan for shutdown, aerosol control, cleaning, disinfection, and restart.

steps.title: Shut down and contain
steps.detail: Isolate electrical and mechanical energy under the site procedure. Establish containment and the approved waste route. Follow site controls for fans, nearby air intakes, and exposure during cleaning.

steps.title: Remove loose deposits
steps.detail: Drain as specified and remove sludge and debris from the basin, strainers, and accessible surfaces. Inspect fill, drift eliminators, distribution nozzles, coatings, and corrosion before choosing a cleaner.

steps.title: Clean for the actual soil
steps.detail: Use the compatible product and approved method for grease, organic soils, or mineral deposits. Apply surface directions to surfaces; use the isolated recirculation method only where the equipment and method permit it.

steps.title: Rinse and complete site disinfection
steps.detail: Capture cleaning waste and verify the rinse endpoint. Complete the separate disinfection procedure specified by the water-management plan using the appropriate registered product and its label; a descaler is not a substitute.

steps.title: Refill, treat, and verify
steps.detail: Inspect and restore equipment, refill with approved water, restart the approved treatment/feed controls, and check leaks and operating readings. Record control measurements and owner approval before routine operation.

guides.stop: If contamination or a Legionella concern is suspected, involve the water-management team and follow its response plan before proceeding. Do not improvise chemical mixtures or disinfection doses.
guides.record: Log shutdown, inspection findings, cleaning product/method, separate disinfection record, waste route, refill chemistry, controller checks, and restart approval.

guides.title: Set up ongoing scale and corrosion control
guides.summary: Use WaterSafe60 within a site-specific treatment plan; cleaning and maintenance treatment have different concentrations and endpoints.
guides.prepare: Identify the system and use: open cooling tower, closed loop, process water, or potable application. Confirm applicable product listing, maximum use level, system restrictions, and current label with the treatment specialist.

steps.title: Characterize the water
steps.detail: Measure makeup and system water chemistry, including the specialist's required hardness, alkalinity, conductivity, pH, temperature, and corrosion indicators. Confirm system volume, makeup demand, blowdown, materials, and existing chemicals.

steps.title: Set the treatment target
steps.detail: Have the treatment specialist select the dose, target residual, control limits, sampling points, and response actions from the current product documentation and site water analysis. Do not use a descaling concentration as a continuous feed setting.

steps.title: Commission the feed
steps.detail: Use compatible metering equipment and containment. Verify pump calibration and controller/probe readings, set the approved feed/interlocks, and confirm the actual treatment response with the specified test or titration method.

steps.title: Monitor and correct
steps.detail: Trend the required residual and water parameters at the site's intervals. Inspect for scale, corrosion, fouling, and leaks. Correct out-of-limit results under the approved plan; record water changes, feed adjustments, and service work.

steps.title: Maintain the full water-management plan
steps.detail: Coordinate scale/corrosion treatment with the site's separate microbiological controls, cleaning schedule, stagnation controls, and shutdown/restart procedures. Review results and responsibilities with the owner.

guides.stop: Escalate unknown water chemistry, loss of feed, unexplained pH change, corrosion, or a water-management control failure. WaterSafe60, HVAC CR, and HVAC HCR do not replace a Legionella water-management program.
guides.record: Keep water analyses, selected dose and control limits, calibration/test records, trend logs, corrective actions, service visits, and the current site plan.
